_note: Original advanced lesson. Language-specific code appears through block variants.
title: Linked Lists
summary: A linked list stores values in nodes, and each node points to the next node.
refresher: A node holds data and a link to the next node. To insert or delete, change links carefully so the list does not lose the rest of itself.

sections.title: The node shape
sections.summary: A node is one value plus one link.

blocks.body: A linked list is not stored by index like an array. You start at the head node and follow `next` links until the list ends.

blocks.caption: The node class is the building block. Value stores data; next points to the next node.

choices: A link to the next node
blocks.why: `next` tells the program which node comes after the current one.

sections.title: Changing links
sections.summary: Insert and delete by rewiring links in the right order.

blocks.body: To insert after a node, point the new node at the old next node first. Then point the current node at the new node. That order keeps the rest of the list reachable.

blocks.caption: The order matters because losing a link can lose the rest of the list.

blocks.prompt: Why save or reuse the old `next` link before overwriting it?
choices: So the rest of the list is not lost
blocks.why: If you overwrite the only link to the rest of the list, those nodes become unreachable.
